title: Clicking with the text tool lands on the grid too
goal: With the grid on, every shape you draw now starts and ends on the grid lines, but clicking with the text tool still drops the text box exactly where the pointer was. A caption placed on graph paper should sit on the paper like everything else.
notes: Found on 2026-09-06 while doing a-shape-you-draw-lands-on-the-grid-like-everythi. CanvasPointerDrags mouseDown line 90: `if tool == .text { beginTextSession(layerID: nil, at: p) }` uses the raw document point and never goes near snappedAnnotationPoint, so no edge magnet and no grid. Text is placed by a CLICK, not a drag, so there is no opposite end and no one cell floor to worry about: it just wants the point quantized. AnnotationSnapping.snap with shape nil and opposite nil already does exactly that (it is what the frame tool uses on its press), so this should be a one line change plus a test. | DONE: CanvasView.snappedTextOrigin(_:event:) asks AnnotationSnapping.snap for a shapeless point with no opposite (grid quantize only, no edge magnet, no floor, no guide, no snap memory in either direction, Command frees). CanvasPointerDrags.swift mouseDown line ~93 passes it to beginTextSession. Re-edit paths (lines 244/252, CanvasKeys 59) still use the layer's own origin, so existing text never moves. Gated by next-canvas-grid through canvasSnapSpacing, so Current is untouched and there is nothing to port.
acceptance: With the grid on, a text box placed by clicking has its top left corner on a grid line
Holding Command while clicking places it exactly where the pointer is
With the grid off, or Snap to grid off, placing text behaves exactly as it does today

log.note: review before building: the mock-free version of this is one quantize. Walked it as a first-time user: with the grid on the caret jumps up to half a cell from the click, same as a shape's first corner, so the tool reads as helping rather than missing. Deliberately took NO edge magnets: text never had them, and a click carries no direction to say which border it meant, so a caption dropped beside a line in the screenshot would jump onto that line's baseline. No one cell floor either: a click has no opposite end. Shortest version wins, nothing else to cut.

TDD: three tests in AnnotationGridSnappingTests (Placing a text block) pin the click contract - shape nil, opposite nil quantizes; free hands the pointer back; nothing pulling leaves it untouched. Then CanvasView.snappedTextOrigin(_:event:) and one line in CanvasPointerDrags mouseDown.

verified in the real app, not assumed. Scripts/playtest/text-on-the-grid-walk.json on the probe: clicked 407,293 -> Text at 416,288; Command-clicked 300,505 -> exactly 300,505; Snap to grid off, clicked 201,611 -> exactly 201,611. Screen Recording was granted so both pictures are real captures. Scripts/test.sh green, 3870 tests.

review after building: the box corner is on the line but the glyphs sit a few points inside it, because a line of type is taller than its letters. Left as is (every design tool snaps the box, and X/Y in the panel agree with the line), raised in the audit for the user to judge.
